assumptions: The founder targets one narrow Polish importer segment and caps concurrent pilots as proposed.
Importers can legally grant the described workflow access and representative mandate, but no willingness to grant either is assumed.
All founder and contractor labor, insurance, security and specialist review are included when testing contribution economics.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Two or more prepaid diagnostics converting into signed implementation and operating agreements, with documented procurement authority, production access, delivery hours, exception load, fully loaded contribution margin, CAC payback, renewal intent and measurable operational improvement would support a higher score.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The redesign correctly identifies the obtainable control point as an importer-specific contracted workflow rather than ownership of compliance or supplier data. This is coherent with the legally contractible representative role and external infrastructure constraints.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: A dated compliance obligation, evidence gaps and buyer-side implementation examples provide a credible purchasing basis. Willingness to buy diagnostics, integration or delegated operations from this prospective business remains unvalidated.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid diagnostics, implementation deposits, retainers and pass-through exception costs improve cash conversion and bound downside. Margins, delivery capacity, CAC, retention and insurance costs remain hypothetical, and the labor component limits operating leverage.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Polish mid-market operators using Odoo or manual workflows form a more focused and reachable beachhead. Its size, commodity concentration and ability to support the founder's wealth target are not yet evidenced.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Local-language exception handling and narrow ERP implementation may win a service niche, but the position is nonexclusive, replaceable and vulnerable to established vendors or ERP implementers adding local service.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: Reusable adapters and playbooks could support expansion across suppliers, commodities, ERP environments and adjacent compliance operations. Customer confidentiality and customer-specific delivery may inhibit reuse and slow scaling.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Embedded workflows, operating history and reusable playbooks can create modest switching costs. Contracts are proposed rather than signed, mandates remain revocable, data reuse is uncertain and incumbents can reproduce the service bundle.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The offer provides a clearer advantage through bounded implementation, Polish-language exception resolution, prepayment and operational accountability. No measured evidence yet shows superior cost, speed, accuracy or trust sufficient to force switching.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: Approaching EUDR application dates and continuing changes to scope, APIs and lifecycle rules create a timely implementation window. Simplification and maturing incumbent products could shorten the opportunity.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: A direct paid diagnostic is a concrete acquisition instrument and avoids dependence on unverified referral partners. The founder still lacks a pipeline, conversion evidence, procurement access and proven CAC compatible with part-time selling.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: A two-pilot cap, light integration and contractor support fit the founder's capital and time better than a platform-first build. Execution still depends on importer signature, access provisioning, supplier truth, official-system onboarding, specialist review and liability controls.

highest_value_structural_change: Secure a repeatable channel or anchor partnership tied to a single ERP-and-commodity niche, with standardized contract terms and implementation artifacts, so customer acquisition and delivery become reproducible rather than founder-specific service work.
main_structural_strength: The model aligns its control point with something legally contractible and pairs it with deposits and pass-through costs that reduce access and working-capital risk.
primary_score_limiter: There is still no signed importer commitment or evidence that direct diagnostics convert into profitable, renewable workflow contracts at sufficient scale.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: Existing vendors offer overlapping supplier, validation, ERP and official-system functionality at low advertised prices, and an authorised-representative mandate neither transfers operator responsibility nor creates durable exclusive control.
